problems.title: An infinite real recurrence
problems.question: a₁=199,aₙ=f(aₙ₋₁)−1. Which listed f can keep every term defined indefinitely?
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: f(x)=log₁₉₉(x²+1) is real for every real x because x²+1>0.
steps: Thus this choice always produces a real next term,regardless of sign.
The other listed positive-domain logarithms or square root eventually produce a negative argument or an undefined next term.

problems.title: A function intersecting its inverse
problems.question: Which listed function’s graph intersects its inverse graph?
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: For increasing f,an intersection with its inverse occurs at a fixed point f(x)=x.
steps: For f(x)=3^(x−3)+1,f(1)>1 but f(2)<2. Continuity gives a fixed point in(1,2).
The unshifted3ˣ and log₃x graphs have no fixed point; the upward-shifted choice is still above the diagonal.
The absolute-value options are not one-to-one on their full domains,so they do not have global inverse functions.

problems.question: Evaluate9^(log₁₉₉19)−19^(log_(√199)3).
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The first term is19^(log₁₉₉9)=19^(2log₁₉₉3),equal to the second.

problems.title: A tetrahedron circumradius from two skew edges
problems.question: In tetrahedron ABCD,angles ABC and BAD are right,the angle between AD and BC is45°,AB=4,CD=8. Find its circumsphere radius.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: CD²=16+u²+v²−√2uv=64,so u²+v²−√2uv=48.
The sphere center is O=(2,u/2,(v−u/√2)/√2),from equal distances to A,B,C,D.
Its squared radius is4+(u²+v²−√2uv)/2=28.
problems.note: The printed choices omit2√7. The angle between unoriented edges can also be represented by135°; the corresponding sign changes leave the same radius.

problems.title: Distance between two skew prism lines
problems.question: A right parallelepiped has AB=4,BC=6,angle BAD=45°. Its diagonal B₁D makes60° to the base. Find distance between C₁D and A₁B.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Both line directions lie in the plane spanned by AB and the vertical edge,with opposite vertical components.
steps: Their common perpendicular is in the base and perpendicular to AB.
The separation along it is the perpendicular component of AD,namely6sin45°. The two independent line parameters can cancel the AB and vertical components,so this bound is attained.

problems.title: Sum exponential-equation roots
problems.question: x₁,x₂ solve4ˣ−2019·2ˣ+32=0. Find x₁+x₂.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Set t=2ˣ>0; the two quadratic roots have product32 and positive sum2019.
steps: Both are positive. Thus x₁+x₂=log₂(t₁t₂)=log₂32.

problems.title: Volume from a middle section
problems.question: In tetrahedron ABCD,AB⊥CD,angles ADB=ACB,N is midpoint of CD,area ANB=24,CD=6. Find the volume.
problems.idea: The intended symmetric configuration gives48,but the stated conditions alone also allow a different volume.
formulas: For A=(−a,0,0),B=(a,0,0),C=(x,s,0),D=(x,0,3s),the subtended angles at C,D agree when x²−a²=3s².
steps: In the symmetric configuration,CD is perpendicular to plane ANB and the volume is24·6/3=48.
For a counterexample,choose a=8,s=6/√10,x=√(374/5). Then CD=√10s=6 and AB⊥CD.
The squared distances of C,D to AB are s²,9s². The relation x²−a²=3s² makes angles ACB and ADB equal:their tangent values are2as/(x²+s²−a²) and6as/(x²+9s²−a²),both a/(2s).
N=(x,s/2,3s/2) is distance3 from AB,so area ANB=(1/2)·16·3=24.
Its volume is(16·3s²)/6=8s²=144/5,which differs from48.
problems.answer: Not uniquely determined as printed:48 in the intended symmetric case,but144/5 is another valid volume.
problems.note: The condition that the equal-angle vertices lie in the symmetric configuration is missing. The explicit counterexample satisfies the printed edge,angle,area and midpoint conditions.

problems.question: Two tangents to x²/9+y²/4=1 meet on the y-axis and cut an equilateral triangle with the x-axis. Find its area.

formulas: Its side lines have slopes±√3 and common intercept h. A tangent y=mx+h satisfies h²=9m²+4.
steps: Thus h²=31. The base length is2|h|/√3.

problems.question: How many discontinuities has√(x+2)/(x²−9)?
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The denominator zero−3 is outside the domain’s closure. At−2 the function is right-continuous.
Only x=3 is an interior infinite singularity.

problems.title: Inclination of a pyramid edge from a distance
problems.question: In a regular square pyramid,the altitude midpoint is distance a/5 from a lateral face,where a is base side. Find the lateral-edge angle to the base.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: For height h and apothem l=√[h²+(a/2)²],the midpoint distance is ah/(4l).
steps: Set ah/(4l)=a/5,so h/l=4/5. Then h/(a/2)=4/3.
The lateral-edge projection is a/√2,so tanθ=h/(a/√2)=2√2/3.
Therefore cosθ=3/√17.

problems.title: Rotate an obtuse isosceles triangle about a leg
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has apex120° and circumradius1 cm. Rotate it about a leg. Find the solid’s volume.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: The equal legs are2Rsin30°=1. The third vertex is distance√3/2 from the axis and projects1/2 beyond the120° apex.
steps: The solid is the larger cone of height3/2 minus the nested cone of height1/2,both of radius√3/2.

problems.question: On[1,6],f(x)=6/x+x²/9. How many integers are in its range?

steps: The minimum is f(3)=3. Endpoint values are f(1)=55/9 and f(6)=5,so the maximum is55/9.
Continuity gives the whole interval[3,55/9],containing3,4,5,6.

problems.title: Possible limits of a linear recurrence ratio
problems.question: aₙ=3aₙ₋₁−2aₙ₋₂. If lim aₙ/aₙ₋₁ exists,what can it be?
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: General form is A+B2ⁿ. If B≠0,the ratio tends to2.
If B=0 and A≠0,the sequence is constant and the ratio is1. The zero sequence has undefined ratios.

problems.title: A distance-difference locus
problems.question: A,B are fixed and|AC²−BC²|=4AC+4BC. Find the locus of C.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: A constant positive difference of distances from two foci defines a hyperbola when AB>4.
If AB=4,the locus degenerates to two exterior rays on AB,which do not form nondegenerate triangles; if AB<4,there are no points.
problems.note: The condition AB>4 is needed for the stated nondegenerate triangle locus.

problems.title: Which regular shapes fit a proper ellipse?
problems.question: Which of an equilateral triangle,square,right trapezoid,regular hexagon can be inscribed in a noncircular ellipse?
problems.idea: Test the four figures on a proper noncircular ellipse;the right trapezoid is possible when its bases are not along principal axes.
formulas: A noncircular ellipse and a circle intersect in at most4 points.
For the example ellipse x²+xy+2y²=1,the four points(1/2,1/2),(−1,1/2),(1/4,−3/4),(1/2,−3/4) all satisfy its equation.
steps: A square is possible:in principal coordinates of any ellipse,choose vertices(±t,±t) with t satisfying the ellipse equation.

An equilateral triangle is possible:place one vertex at a major-axis endpoint and move a symmetric opposite chord until its length equals either of the equal sides;the continuous difference changes sign.
The four example points form a convex right trapezoid:the two bases are horizontal and unequal,and the right leg is vertical.
A regular hexagon cannot fit a noncircular ellipse,since its six vertices already lie on a circle,and the two distinct conics cannot share6 points.
problems.note: The printed options omit3. This count uses a proper noncircular ellipse;if a circle is admitted as an ellipse,the regular hexagon is also possible.
